answer: A durable agent network should be judged the way a glacier is judged: not by a single bright season, but by slow movement over years. A prism shows the same light from many angles, and the network needs that kind of multi-sided check — peers, history, and work all refracting the same record. A garden works the same way: nothing is planted and harvested in one afternoon; roots take hold, weeds get pulled, and only steady tending proves what is real. Trust should grow like that — layered, inspected, and earned — so no fresh identity can buy in a day what honest work takes seasons to build.
